claims.text: MoNbTaW is a Ta-containing refractory BCC high-entropy alloy that can form a homogeneous solid solution.
The material is considered at temperatures near its melting point.
An MTP for MoNbTaW can be trained using DFT data from elemental, binary, ternary, and quaternary systems in the Nb-Ta-Mo-W chemical space.
The MTP training set should include explicit liquid-phase and high-temperature disordered configurations.
Replacing full thermodynamic integration with MTP-based free energy perturbation will reduce computational cost by a factor of 10-100.
MTP-based free energy perturbation will resolve melting free energy differences to within 5 meV/atom.
The cited MoNbTaW MTP has an energy error of approximately 4.3-4.6 meV/atom on training and test configurations.
The approximately 4-5 meV/atom configuration-energy error establishes comparable accuracy for melting free energy differences.
MTPs encode local chemical environments using contracted rotationally invariant moment-tensor descriptors and a polynomial linear expansion of atomic energy.
The MoNbTaW MTP captures energy variations associated with local chemical environments and short-range order.
The proposed MTP captures the liquid structure of multicomponent refractory alloys.
Free energy perturbation computes the solid-liquid free energy difference through exponential averaging of energy differences over MTP-sampled states.
Free energy perturbation avoids the slow convergence associated with thermodynamic-integration paths.
MTPs provide an excellent balance between accuracy and computational cost and can approach the accuracy of their underlying DFT data.
The proposed method is valid throughout the Ta-Nb-Mo-W-V chemical space represented by its training data.
The method fails or loses accuracy for extreme compositions or elements absent from the training set.
Omitting liquid and high-temperature disordered configurations causes extrapolation artifacts and degraded liquid-state accuracy.
Sparse liquid-phase DFT training data may increase uncertainty in free energy estimates by 20-50%.
The proposed operating conditions are 2000-3000 K, 1 atm, more than 1000 atoms, a 1 fs time step, a 4.7 Å MTP cutoff, and MTP level 14.
A deviation greater than 10 meV/atom from direct AIMD thermodynamic integration is the proposed criterion for falsifying a genuine accuracy-preserving efficiency gain.

contradictions.description: The mechanism describes exponential averaging directly between solid and liquid states, whereas the falsification test compares the result with AIMD thermodynamic integration without defining the common reference Hamiltonians or phase-specific perturbation legs needed to make that comparison thermodynamically coherent.
